citations.claim: initial total energy before close heavy-body approach
total energy at first violating step has drifted by ~108 beyond allowance
heavy body 3 reaches high speed as bodies 3 and 4 close to 0.56 separation

counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 0.03333 to 0.001 with all bodies, G, seed and steps unchanged; finer integration resolves the close heavy-body encounter and removes the energy drift

explanation: Two 20-mass bodies start ~1.12 apart and fall toward each other while light bodies add strong nearby forces. With large dt=1/30 the 6 adaptive substeps per outer step are insufficient as separation shrinks to 0.95 at step 1 then 0.56 at step 2 and speeds reach ~10; leapfrog energy error accumulates (~6 at step1 then ~108 by step2) exceeding the 2% tolerance. Reducing only dt to 0.001 keeps energy constant, confirming temporal resolution / substepping insufficiency during the close heavy-body encounter.
vision_note: Two large bodies start very close together and move toward each other from step 0 to step 1. By step 2 they nearly overlap in a close encounter while the three smaller bodies stay almost stationary.
